title: Normative and Clinical Validation Study of Neuropsychological Tasks Implemented in EpiTrack Junior for the Assessment of Figural and Verbal Memory
summary:
Children and adolescents with epilepsy often experience difficulties in various aspects of thinking and learning. In addition to problems with attention and concentration, memory functions may also be impaired. These difficulties can affect both academic performance and everyday life.

The aim of this study is to extend an established neuropsychological screening instrument for children and adolescents (EpiTrack Junior). Two new tasks assessing verbal and figural memory will be added to the test battery. The objectives are to establish age-appropriate normative data for these new tasks and to evaluate whether the extended instrument can reliably identify memory difficulties in children and adolescents with epilepsy.

The study will include healthy children and adolescents as well as children and adolescents with epilepsy aged 6 to under 18 years. Participants will complete the EpiTrack Junior, including the new memory tasks, in an individual assessment lasting approximately 20 minutes. A subset of participants will be reassessed after approximately three months to evaluate the reliability of the instrument.

The long-term goal of the study is to develop a brief and practical tool for assessing important cognitive functions in children and adolescents with epilepsy.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Healthy children and adolescents (normative sample) or children and adolescents with epilepsy (clinical validation sample)
- Attendance at a mainstream school
- Written informed consent from a parent or legal guardian
- Age-appropriate assent from the child or adolescent
Exclusion criteria:
- Known epilepsy (for participants in the normative sample)
- Known neurological disorders or chronic medical conditions involving the central nervous system
- Known intellectual disability (IQ < 70 and/or special educational needs related to intellectual development)
- Inability to cooperate sufficiently or to complete the assessment, as determined by the investigator
- Insufficient German language proficiency that would interfere with understanding the test instructions, as determined by the investigator
